Other routes have seen similar jumps, with the cost of transporting oil from Brazil to China surging by a third over the past week, according to shipbroker Braemar.
The war in Iran has caused a severe shortage of some of the world’s largest tankers, which hold ~2M barrels, because ships have been forced to redraw their routes and travel much longer distances.
"Freight rates have gone parabolic," Energy Aspects founder Amrita Sen told
. "Freight may well be the thing that breaks this market in the near term, as landed crude costs in Asia have soared towards $150/bbl."

The surging cost of transporting oil has forced some refineries to start cutting production as their profitability falls, even as the price of refined fuels also hits record highs; diesel prices in Singapore have reached $180/bbl and well over $200/bbl in Europe.

"Shipping is no longer a marginal cost in oil markets—it is becoming a defining price driver," Argus head of oil market analysis Tom Reed said. "Freight charges now account for around a fifth of the cost of delivering crude to refineries, highlighting how disruption at sea is increasingly feeding directly into the delivered price of oil."
Meanwhile, Brent crude prices have dropped back to ~$100/bbl this week, well below theirwartime high above $125 in April.

for October delivery bounced 1.4% to $91.74/bbl, after both benchmarks fell for five straight sessions.
